@thdxr @fwang — I respect what both of you have built. OpenCode Go has been the best value-for-money coding API I have used, and I have recommended it to everyone I know.

But this Alibaba content-filtering situation is a deal-breaker, and it needs your attention directly.

GLM-5.2 via opencode-go is now **effectively unusable** for me. It is not intermittent. It is not recoverable with a retry. After the first few content-filter rejections, my account appears to be **permanently blacklisted at the IP or request-header level by Alibaba Cloud's filter** — every single GLM-5.2 request now fails immediately with the "inappropriate content" error, regardless of what the actual prompt contains. I cannot use the model I am paying for.

This is not a "rate limit" issue. This is not a "quota" issue. This is Alibaba Cloud reading my prompts and deciding I am a bad actor, with zero transparency into what triggered the filter, zero appeal process, and zero way to opt out of Alibaba routing.

Let me be blunt: **you are routing paying users' private prompts through a third-party cloud provider that performs server-side content scanning, without any disclosure, ToS, or opt-out anywhere in the product.** If DeepInfra, Fireworks, or ZhipuAI official started doing this tomorrow, people would leave overnight. The only reason this has not blown up yet is that most users have not hit the filter — yet.

If removing Alibaba from the routing pool is not feasible in the short term, at minimum we need:
1. An immediate way to opt out of Alibaba routing per model or per account
2. Clear disclosure in the OpenCode Go dashboard showing which upstream a model request was routed to
3. A published ToS that honestly describes content handling

I want to keep using and recommending OpenCode Go. Please do not make that impossible.

Quick clarification to my previous comment — "permanently blacklisted at IP level" was too strong. Let me be more precise:

- On OpenCode (regular dev work): GLM-5.2 works fine for normal coding tasks. The filter only triggers when the prompt happens to hit Alibaba's upstream and contains content their scanner flags.
- The issue is specifically that **once flagged, subsequent requests from the same session/account appear to be rejected at the header level** (token or session fingerprint), not IP. Creating a fresh session/token resolves it — until the next flag.
- This means the filter has a **ratcheting effect**: one flagged request poisons the session, and the user has no way to know which upstream they hit or how to reset.

So the practical impact is:
- Light coding use → usually fine, but with a non-deterministic failure surface
- Any use case with content that might trigger Alibaba's scanner → a single flagged request cascades to session-wide rejection
- OpenCode Go users have zero way to know which requests route through Alibaba vs. other upstreams

Still a serious problem, but not total account death — sorry for the overstatement. The core ask doesn't change: transparency and opt-out.

One more data point on what triggers Alibaba's filter — my game project https://github.com/WhiteGiverMa/odyssey-cards contains some mature-themed narrative text. When GLM-5.2 processes files from this repo via OpenCode Go and hits the Alibaba upstream, the request is rejected with the "inappropriate content" error.

This is a strategy card game — not a pure adult game, not spam, not abuse. It is a creative work with some mature elements in its storytelling, exactly the kind of project where a large-context reasoning model would be most valuable for world-building and narrative design.

The broader point: **if AI-assisted creative writing — including writing with mature themes — is treated as a violation by an upstream provider, then OpenCode Go's routing policy is silently closing off entire categories of legitimate software development.** A visual novel dev, a game writer, anyone building interactive fiction with adult themes — all of them would hit this wall without ever knowing why, because OpenCode Go has no published policy warning them.

This is not about asking Alibaba to change their ToS. It is about OpenCode Go deciding whether its routing architecture should respect the creative freedom of its users, or silently delegate that decision to the most restrictive upstream in the pool.

Fixed.

 Root cause: your shell had these in ~/.zshrc:

 ```sh
   export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080
   export OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8080
 ```

 That forced OpenCode’s OpenAI provider to call localhost:8080 instead of OpenAI, so OAuth was
 valid but every OpenAI model returned immediate reason:"error" with 0 tokens.

The idea was custom subagents pinned to that model so the primary agent automatically delegates cheap work locally, saving cloud tokens. The model config on custom agents works fine, they load correctly. The missing piece is `subagent_type` accepting custom agent names.

#20019: closely related, but this appears to be a different failure mode in a different tool path. It covers _plugin_ tools where omitted optional/defaulted args become `undefined` or `{}`, so defaults are not applied.

This issue is about _MCP tools_ where omitted optional args appear to become explicit empty/default values, especially `[]`. That changes the request semantics.

So the desired behavior here is not simply “coerce missing args to {}” or “apply defaults.” It is: preserve omitted optional fields as omitted inside tools/call.arguments, unless the schema explicitly defines a default and that default is intentionally applied.

#20637: related, but distinct in that it also concerns MCP optional-argument handling, but it describes a different failure mode. That one is about an MCP tool where **all** parameters are optional and OpenCode rejects a call with no `tool_use.input`. The desired behavior there is to allow a no-argument tool call.

These issues may share code around optional tool argument normalization, but the required behavior is different for each one:
1. normalize a missing top-level tool input to {} when needed
2. do not expand omitted optional properties inside arguments into "", 0, or [] unless the schema explicitly defines and intentionally applies such defaults.

Related issue: opencode serve API transfer extremely slow with large session JSON (300MB+)

I'm experiencing a similar issue but specifically with the opencode serve HTTP API.

Symptoms:

When calling GET /session/:id or GET /session/:id/message, the response takes a very long time to transfer
The session JSON is over 300MB in size
There is no way to filter out fields or limit the response payload
Root cause appears to be the same:

Base64-encoded attachments (images, PDFs, etc.) are stored inline in the session/message JSON
The API returns the full JSON without any field filtering option
What I've tried:

GET /session/:id/message?limit=10 — this helps for listing messages, but the session detail endpoint (/session/:id) still returns the full payload
There's no ?fields= or ?exclude= query parameter available
Suggestion: It would be helpful if the API supported one of the following:

Field filtering (e.g., ?exclude=attachments or ?fields=id,title,createdAt)
Store attachments externally (as proposed in PR #34011) and reference them by ID
Add a ?summary=true option that returns session metadata without inline attachments
This is a blocker for anyone using opencode serve programmatically with large sessions.

Research update from team discussion:

- Prefer keeping the Node runtime on built-in `node:sqlite` if possible.
- The main concern with adopting `better-sqlite3` is packaging across all OpenCode targets.
- This makes the likely direction: use Drizzle's official Effect SQLite adapter/query layer where it helps, but keep or upstream a small `node:sqlite` Effect `SqlClient` instead of switching the OpenCode Node path to `better-sqlite3` by default.

Direction update:

Given the packaging concern around `better-sqlite3`, we should likely **keep OpenCode's existing built-in `node:sqlite` implementation** for 2.0.

Re-scope this from "replace our custom implementation" to a smaller research/porting task:

- Compare Drizzle rc.4+ official Effect SQLite internals against `packages/effect-drizzle-sqlite` and our runtime SQLite layers.
- Identify anything worth porting, especially around SQLite session/query execution, typed errors, migrations, cache invalidation, optimized mappers/JIT behavior, and non-interactive Drizzle Kit workflows.
- Avoid switching the Node path to `better-sqlite3` by default.
- Keep deletion of the vendored adapter as optional only if we can do it without losing the built-in `node:sqlite` packaging/runtime path.

As a happy Go subscriber, I don't know about what the confusing UX of paying for Zen vs subscribing to Go was, but I'd like to clarify that there's no separate *API key* for Zen vs Go. Your API key works for *both* Zen and Go; whatever gets used (if you have the respective balance / subscription activated) depends on whether you selected OpenCode Zen or OpenCode Go in the UI of the OpenCode application itself – you don't configure it per-API-key in the opencode.ai web. And if the toggle `Use your available balance after reaching the usage limits` is on, your OpenCode Zen balance (if you have one in addition to your OpenCode Go subscription) can be used even if you configured OpenCode Go, but only *when you have reached the OpenCode Go usage limits*.

Just wanted to clarify this because you mentioned Go vs Zen API keys, so I wanted to clear up the confusion.

@zcutlip OMP has served me well, still not perfect but I stick with it for now. A feature related to multi-provider setup that I liked is the ability to select canonical models, i.e. a model name without a provider prefix. I want GLM-5.2, don't care about which provider. Configure your providers sorting order (`modelProvidingOrder`. OMP also supports equivalence, so you can say `deepseek/deekseek-v4-pro` is equivalent to `glm-5.2` (for example) then have `deepseek` at the end of the providers preference, it lets deepseek-v4-pro becomes a final fallback option when glm-5.2 can't be served by any.

Unfortunately OMP doesn't switch automatically. But you can live-switch the provider mid-session after an error so recovery isn't that bad. OMP also supports cross-model reasoning recovery.
